Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8169732
Permit API: 129-27066
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/27/2023
Comments: December 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to the spill reported to the Department on 10/20/2023 (CTS: 375673). According to the operator, the spill was approximately 40 barrels of production fluid, released from the valve near the bottom of the production tank. The initial inspection of the spill is documented in IR 3636824. The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the production tank appeared to be removed from the site and it appeared that excavation of the contaminated material had begun. The area of excavation was approximately 30 feet by 30 feet and roughly 5.5 feet in depth. The Department took conductivity readings at the bottom of the excavated area with readings of 0.02mS, 0.12mS, and 0.18mS. It appeared that all of the excavated material was still on site, in several piles surrounding the excavated hole. In some areas, it appeared sediment had begun to travel downslope from the piles. Upon further inspection, it appeared that no E and S BMPs were implemented anywhere on the site. The Department recommends the operator promptly install E and S BMPs to prevent further migration of sediment and to minimize the potential for further sedimentation to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to implement E and S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Previous violations associated with the release remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-01-22 to Jklm Energy Llc in Sweden Twp, Potter county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Jklm Energy Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-01-22
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 839700
Permit API: 105-21888
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Sweden Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-22
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCDT inspection of the JKLM Sweden Valley 106 Well Pad located in Sweden Twp, Potter Co. on 1/22/2019 @1130 hours. The weather was 16 degrees, overcast, winds S@9mph. Approximately 12" of snow was deposited onsite in the previous 72 hours. JKLM representative Scott West and DEP Env Trainee, Korey Starkey was present onsite. JKLM contractor Pro Frac is currently stimulating the 6 utica wells onsite. Mr. West stated at the time of this inspection they had just completed stimulating stage 13 of the 2HU well, and perforating stage 7 of the 5HU well. Two small spills have been reported within the last week on the SV 106 well site, during the frack. Spill #1 (CTS#339324), occurred and was reported on 1/16/2019. The spill reportedly involved the release of 400 to 500 gallons of brine from the working tank. The spill was reportedly mostly on primary containment with some spray hitting the perimeter of the pad. As of today's inspection the secondary containment around the working tanks was full of snow. One area in the containment, which appeared to be a high foot traffic area, had slush/fluid mix with a field measure conductivity of "Over Range". A vac truck was dispatched to remove the fluid. The containment had recently been repaired in the same area. No melted slush or fluid was observed outside of containment. Additional screening, when conditions allow, under and around the secondary containment was discussed with a representative from Whipper Hill Consulting while onsite. Spill #2 (CTS#339357), occurred and was reported on 1/18/2019. This spill involved the reported release of a few hundred gallons of produced water into containment from a pump filter. The containment berm was compressed allowing 20-30 gallons of produced water to leave the containment impacting the pad surface. As of today's inspection the area along the perimeter of the compromised containment where the spill occurred was snow covered. No melted or stained areas were observed. An onsite representative from Whipper Hill Consulting provided grid drawings of pre and post excavation soil conductivity readings of the impacted area. The highest recorded soil conductivity reading was 1.44mS/cm, the remaining readings were <1.0mS/cm. Excavated materials were placed in waste containers and staged inside containment awaiting disposal. Violations of 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(B) and SWMA 301 are cited as Immediate Corrected at this time. Please address any deficiencies noted and contact me with any questions. I departed the site at 1300 hours. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 369324

Violation ID: 8231114
Permit API: 063-32778
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/24/2025
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 4/16/2025 that Diversified used farm fields to plug an abandoned well, and they did not sufficiently remediate the area. The complaint is associated with Diversified Production, LLC's Margaret E Beck 2 well site (063-32778). This well was drilled in June 2001. The well was plugged in April 2025 by NextLvL. Brian Shank (WQSS) and I completed a Complaint Inspection on 4/24/2025. The lower half of the access road was exposed soil, and upper half of the access road was seeded and mulched. The exposed, steep portion of the access road was not stabilized. There were deep ruts on the exposed, steep portion of the access road and in the seeded/mulched area of the access road. These ruts create channels down the slope of the access road and the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation (E and S). Violations will be cited for failure to implement E and S BMPs. There appeared to be a release from the pit during plugging. There was evidence of material flowing over the silt sock into the neighboring pasture, and the cows licking the area due to the salt content.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8206009
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: On 2/4/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 10 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. Due to frozen conditions, conductivity readings were not taken during this inspection.When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Mark McCormick who described current operations as follows. Drilling to total depth has been completed on eight new gas wells at the site. Crews were on site, prepping for upcoming stimulation operations on the eight wells. Frac equipment was being mobilized to the location. Fracking has not commenced but is expected to start on 2/12/2026 depending on when the crew finishes on the DCNR 007 L Pad and depending on weather. Mark expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by the end of June 2026. In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Three sand separators remain near the wells but have been disconnected.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water/ice. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 0930 hours.

Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Comments: On 10/27/25 I was at the Coterra Energy Lauer D. Well Site from 1327 to 1459 hours to perform a follow up inspection in response to the report a release of an unknown volume of natural gas and production fluid out of the Lauer D 12H well on 10/22/25. The weather conditions are mostly sunny skies with a light wind and temperatures in the low to mid 50's. The intent of the inspection is to evaluate the impact to the ground surface of the well pad from the release of production fluid. Shortly after arrival I met with Brendon Logan, Environmental Health and Safety Specialist. We walked to the location on the site where a sump (Sump # 1) was constructed on 10/22/25 in a drainage channel adjacent to and west of the access road near the well pad entrance. Sump # 1 is collecting fluid which released out of the 12H well onto the well pad and flowed into a drainage channel on the western side of the pad. Fluid in Sump # 1 is transferred via a pump into a frac tank in a containment structure. I utilized a Hanna HI 98331 Groline Soil Test Meter and an Oakton PCTS 5 meter to perform field screening of specific conductance (electrical conductivity, EC) in wet soil in the drainage channel adjacent to Sump #1 and in fluid pooled in this sump. Mr. Logan and I walked in a counter clockwise direction starting in the infiltration basin south of the well pad and in between the tank pad and well pad around the perimeter of the pad in the basin, to the northeast corner of the pad, then across the north side of the pad, and then to the center of the pad near the wells. I also performed conductivity screening in wet soil and fluid in the infiltration basin south and east of the well pad inside of the LOD and on the pad surface near the wells and equipment designated for frac operations. Conductivity readings in fluid in Sump # 1 and in a sump constructed just east and adjacent to the access road and south of the well pad in an infiltration basin, (Sump#2), and on the well pad, are indicative of a spill of production fluid. I also met with Brody Webster, Andy Mehalko, and Mike Oakley of Coterra during the inspection. Coterra is in the process of preparing to remediate (clean up) impacted pad material in association with the release of production fluid. Coterra has removed a section of the secondary containment liner near the wells and rig mats in order to evaluate the extent of the impact and remove impacted material. Coterra informed me that they plan to remove additional equipment designated for frac operations and commence the remediation process via the use of heavy equipment tomorrow, 10/29/25. See photos for additional details. Please feel free to contact me @ 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov should you have any questions.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 2/23/2023 at 0935 hours. The weather was 37 degrees with fog. A layer of snow covered the majority of the site today. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in to the DEP by Repsol on 2/16/2023. On 2/16/2023 at 0900 hours, a release of 18.7 gallons of produced water mixed with sand was released to the pad surface and containment from a sand trap. Repsol promptly called in the release to the DEP reporting hotline and began cleanup activities. A Repsol representative provided photos of the cleanup to me via email on 2/22/2023.During today's inspection, the impacted area was observed to have been excavated. All impacted material recovered was placed into containers for later disposal. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. Pooled water in and around the impacted area was field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 160 to 320us/cm. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #370057 is tied to this release within CTS.Based on the reported release of 18.7 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and containment, violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 are cited against API #117-22124. However, due to Repsol's timely remediation of the reported release, these violations are considered immediately corrected at this time. Violations from a previous issue cited on 8/10/2022 and 9/2/2022 remain outstanding against API #117-22124. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Violation ID: 8275337
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

On 10/12/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued as outstanding for the observed elevated conductivity and the access road condition. The following was observed during inspection on 10/16/2023:The operator had removed impacted soils within the bottom portion of the berm, adjacent to the valve of tank 4. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 1-6). The operator had placed the impacted soils within buckets that were dated (Photos 7, 8).Some soils were removed from the berm adjacent to tank 5. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 9, 10).Regarding the area behind tank 5, it appeared as though the area I initially discovered to have elevated readings, and the operator was not able to replicate my readings, displayed adequate readings on 10/16/23, most likely due to dilution from rain (Photos 11, 12). There was one reading of 3.29 m/S, however this area was small, approximately a 4 inch by 4 inch section (Photo 13). The operator is going to remove some soils from this area, which was marked with a brick (Photo 14). Due to the size of this area, no violation is being noted.The operator explained that the cause of the impacted berm was due to fluids reaching the ground during tank clean out (Photos 15, 16). It is highly recommended to place containment/grate to collect any residual fluids and prevent them from reaching the ground and berm during tank clean out.The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 17, 18). On 10/13/2023, I had emailed Daniel Frick of Diversified regarding the start time of repairs; Diversified is waiting on bids and can hopefully update me next week (from 10/13 email). As of 10/16/2023, there has not been an update. Also in this email, I had asked if the NOV response for IR 3620008, mentioning the removal of a 5 gallon bucket, was referring to the area under the valve of tank 4 instead of behind tank 5, which was then confirmed to be correct - the material was removed from under the valve. Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 847457
Permit API: 123-26419
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-04-10
Comments: This inspection was performed in response to the report of a small release of production fluid along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. Rick Engelbert, with Irvine Run Resources, contacted the Department to report a broken pipeline which resulted in the release of approximately ½ of a barrel of crude oil, to the ground along Irvine Run. The spill was reported to have been contained and was actively being cleaned up. The spill was reported to have been discovered at 14:30, on April 8, 2019. The spill was immediately responded upon by the operator. Legree 30, (37-123-26419): Upon receiving notification of this incident, I contacted Rick to arrange a site visit. I arrived on site at approximately 13:00 on April 10, 2019 to conduct a site investigation. The spill appeared to have occurred as previously described. Production fluid was released from a broken fitting on a buried gathering line. The spill allegedly occurred while the well was being pumped. Crude oil was noticed to have been seeping from the stream bank, approximately 40 feet below the damaged fitting. A small amount of fluid did travel down stream from the discharge point. Pumping was immediately stopped. Approximately 1.5 cubic yards of soil had been excavated around the damaged fitting. There did not appear to be any contaminated soil left in the hole. There did not appear to be all that much contaminated soil even in the material that had been excavated. The area on the stream bank where the fluid was noticed to have been emerging was just above the stream channel. There was no clearly exposed conduit or outlet, only an area of soil that was slightly saturated with crude oil. Small amounts of emulsified oil could be seen pooling in water as far as 80 feet down stream of the original discharge point. Much of the oil appeared to have been absorbed and/or contained by a series of absorbent pads and booms that the operator had placed along the channel. There did not appear to have been any oil at all pooling behind the final boom in the series, approximately 120 feet down-stream of the discharge point. I advised that the operator construct a small syphon dam directly in front of the initial point of discharge, and to continue changing pads and booms as needed. Clean-up progress will be monitored with future inspections.
